If f(x)=x²e^x, what is f′(1)?

A. e
B. 3e
C. e²
D. 2+e

rationales.A: Differentiates only the exponential factor and leaves x² unchanged, giving x²e^x, which equals e at x=1.
rationales.B: Correctly applies the product rule and evaluates.
rationales.C: Confuses evaluation at 1 with squaring e.
rationales.D: Adds derivatives without preserving the product factors.

Which statement is always true?

A. Every continuous function is differentiable.
B. A function with a derivative of 0 at x=a has a local extremum there.
C. A function can be differentiable where it is discontinuous.
D. If a function is differentiable at x=a, then it is continuous there.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a function is differentiable at x=a, then it is continuous there.

rationales.A: A corner can be continuous but not differentiable.
rationales.B: A horizontal tangent need not be an extremum.
rationales.C: Differentiability cannot occur at a discontinuity.

stem: A particle moves along a line with position s(t) = t^2 feet at time t seconds. The average velocity of the particle over the interval [2, 2 + h] is 4 + h feet per second. What is the instantaneous velocity of the particle at t = 2?

rationales.A: Letting h approach 0 shrinks the interval, but it does not make the velocity 0. The expression 4 + h approaches 4.
rationales.B: This uses the time t = 2 as if it were the velocity. The velocity is found from the limit of the average velocity, not read off the time.
rationales.C: The instantaneous velocity is the limit of the average velocity as h approaches 0. As h approaches 0, 4 + h approaches 4.
rationales.D: This is the average velocity over an interval of length h, so it depends on h. The instantaneous velocity is the limit of that expression as h approaches 0.

stem:
The table gives the average rate of change of a function f over the interval [1, 1 + h] for three values of h.

h = 0.1: 6.3
h = 0.01: 6.03
h = 0.001: 6.003

Which of the following is the best estimate of the instantaneous rate of change of f at x = 1?

rationales.A: This is the average rate over the smallest interval in the table. It is close to the target but is still an average over an interval of length 0.001, not the value the averages approach.
rationales.B: This is only the average rate over the widest interval. It is the least accurate of the three values, not the value being approached.
rationales.C: As the interval shrinks, the average rates are 6.3, 6.03, 6.003, moving toward 6. The instantaneous rate is the value these averages approach.
rationales.D: Shrinking the interval toward length 0 does not make the rate 0. The averages in the table are getting closer to 6.

stem: On x²+xy+y²=7, what is dy/dx at (1,2)?

rationales.A: This is the reciprocal of the correct slope (−4/5), not the slope itself.
rationales.B: Implicit differentiation gives 2x+y+(x+2y)y′=0, so y′=−4/5 at (1,2).
rationales.C: The sign from moving 2x+y is missing.
rationales.D: Both sign and reciprocal are incorrect.
